title: Panzanella
subtitle: Italian tomato salad with toasted breadcrumbs, olives, and capers
excerpt: Panzanella is a Tuscan summer salad built on very ripe tomatoes, olive oil, and torn bread. This version uses toasted panko breadcrumbs in place of torn loaf, giving a lighter crunch. The dressing soaks into everything and makes it intensely savoury.
sourceNotes: Panzanella is a traditional Tuscan salad, historically a dish for using up stale bread in summer. It is popular across central Italy and varies slightly by region.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress up to 30 minutes ahead so the tomatoes release juice into the dressing. Do not make hours ahead or the crumbs will go soft.

content.text: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. A mix of sizes and colours works well. The quality of the olive oil matters here too. Use something you would happily put on bread.

items.prepNote: very ripe, mixed sizes, halved or roughly torn
toasted in a dry pan until golden

content.text: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until golden. Set aside to cool.
Make the dressing: whisk the garlic, red wine vinegar, and olive oil together. Season with salt and pepper.
Put the tomatoes in a large bowl. Season with salt and pour over the dressing. Toss and leave for 10 minutes.
Add the capers, olives, and basil. Toss gently.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs over the top. Serve straight away.

items.symptom: The breadcrumbs have gone soft and lost their crunch.
items.cause: They were added too early and absorbed tomato liquid.
items.fix: Always scatter breadcrumbs just before serving.

items.symptom: The salad tastes flat and under-seasoned.
items.cause: Tomatoes were not salted before dressing, or dressing was too light.
items.fix: Season tomatoes first, then dress with more vinegar and salt.
